$comment: Taxonomy-valued fields carry an x-taxonomy annotation naming the dimension in factory/policies/taxonomy.yml. The runtime validates those values against that file at write time; enums are never inlined here to avoid drift between the schema and the taxonomy (architecture §8).
title: Review Finding
description: One reviewer/verifier finding. Verifier's mandate is to refute, not confirm (architecture §6); a finding survives only with a concrete failure scenario (agent-interviews.md V-2).

epic_id.description: The epic this finding belongs to. Optional, not required: findings raised before this field existed carry the epic in the task_id prefix instead, and a task_id that names no epic yields no epic_id rather than a guessed one (D-49/P9-10).

fingerprint.description: Stable hash identifying this finding for dedup and waiver lookup; waived findings are suppressed in future reviews of the same code by fingerprint match.

file_path.description: Repo-relative path the finding is anchored to, normalized (forward slashes, no leading ./). The fingerprint's first component, kept as a field because a hash cannot be joined against a task's claims: dispatch-time context and the stale-evidence check both need the path itself (P9-15).

finding_scope.description: Absent means `diff` — findings written before the dimension existed carry no scope. `spec` says the code is right and the plan is wrong; such a finding blocks the plan, never the diff (P9-9/D-33), and requires spec_ref.

spec_ref.description: Which criterion of which plan version the spec finding is against. Required when finding_scope is `spec` and forbidden otherwise — enforced in findings.ts, not here, because a JSON-Schema `if/then` would have to inline the taxonomy value `spec` (see $comment).

failure_scenario.description: Concrete inputs -> wrong output. A finding without one dies at verify (agent-interviews.md V-2).

same_mistake_of_lesson_id.description: Set when this finding matches an approved lesson; auto-escalates one severity level (architecture §9.7).

waiver_id.description: Set once an S3/S4 finding has been waived by the operator; keyed by fingerprint, never re-asked.

amends_task_ids.description: Set once an amendment took this finding to `amend-pending`: the task ids that amendment added or superseded. They are the finding's discharge condition — until they land it cannot reach `amended`. Without them an amendment closes an unwaivable S1/S2 spec finding at plan-write time, naming no task outcome at all (D-127).

amends_plan_version.description: The plan version that amendment cut, so `amends_task_ids` can be resolved against the version that defines them (D-127).
